body.text: Across modern technology, few developments carry as much structural weight as Confidential Computing. When examined through the lens of architecture and bottlenecks, the gap between surface-level headlines and operational reality becomes unmistakable.

Rather than treating Confidential Computing as an isolated upgrade, leading researchers and operators integrate it into a cohesive system. Every design choice involves explicit trade-offs between throughput, resilience, and simplicity.
Core Principles of Architecture and Bottlenecks

items: Constraint-First Design: Measure real bottlenecks around Confidential Computing before committing capital or engineering cycles.
Empirical Verification: Benchmark architecture and bottlenecks against established baselines rather than vendor claims.
Operational Resilience: Build redundancy and clear observability into every layer touching Confidential Computing.
Compounding Returns: Prioritize incremental, verifiable improvements that hold up over multi-year horizons.
